These issues describe the same root cause — the MCP client sending `Accept: */*` (or an incomplete value) instead of the spec-required `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, causing Spring Boot and other strict MCP servers to reject the request. If the fix from those issues did not address your specific version or scenario, please add details there or reference them.

**Update — root cause found, upstream fix open, and there are builds you can try.**

### What's actually wrong

bun ships **no baseline macOS build**. `@oven/bun-darwin-x64-baseline` is byte-identical to `@oven/bun-darwin-x64` (both the AVX2 build), which is why opencode's `-baseline` Mac binary is too. That's because oven-sh/WebKit never builds a baseline macOS WebKit — `bun-webkit-macos-amd64-baseline.tar.gz` returns **HTTP 404**.

opencode's own packaging is fine — `build.ts` requests `bun-darwin-x64-baseline` correctly; there just isn't a real one upstream.

Full evidence: oven-sh/bun#34206

### Upstream fix (open now)

- **oven-sh/WebKit#290** — builds the missing baseline macOS WebKit
- **oven-sh/bun#34207** — makes bun ship a real `darwin-x64-baseline` (draft; gated on the WebKit PR)

### Builds you can try today

👉 **https://github.com/tobocop2/opencode-bun-pre-avx2-mac/releases/latest**

I built a baseline bun and compiled opencode against it:

| binary | AVX2 (`ymm`) instructions |
|---|---|
| shipped `opencode-darwin-x64-baseline` | 248,019 |
| **this build** | **14,407** |
| `@oven/bun-linux-x64-baseline` *(verified working on real pre-AVX2 hardware)* | 12,328 |

### I need testers — I couldn't test this on a real Mac

No cloud provider rents a pre-AVX2 Intel Mac, so I verified the recipe on a pre-AVX2 **linux** box instead (the baseline runs `opencode run` to completion there; the AVX2 build crashes after ~21s / ~3.9 GB). **If you have one of these Macs, I'd genuinely appreciate a report either way:**

```bash
chmod +x opencode-darwin-x64-baseline
./opencode-darwin-x64-baseline --version
```

Unofficial builds — not affiliated with oven-sh or anomalyco, just a stopgap until the PRs land.

Confirming @tobocop2's root cause from the other side — a genuinely pre-AVX CPU. I hit this on a Xeon X5690 (Westmere, 2010): no AVX at all, only up to SSE4.2, so it's a strictly harder case than the Ivy Bridge / AVX1 machines above.

Same diagnosis: bun's own C/C++/Rust is built correctly for `-march=nehalem`, but the "baseline" macOS x64 build links the **Haswell** WebKit, whose bmalloc startup constructors contain BMI2/AVX2 (`shlx` / `bzhi` / `blsr`). Those run in a C++ static initializer *before* `main()`, so it SIGILLs at startup. oven-sh/WebKit ships no Nehalem/baseline macOS tarball, which is why the "baseline" label is currently ineffective on macOS (also tracked in oven-sh/bun#32512).

One thing worth flagging for oven-sh/WebKit#290 and oven-sh/bun#34207: **clearing the startup SIGILL is necessary but not sufficient.** I built bun from source with `--baseline=true --webkit=local` (`-march=nehalem`, WebKit compiled locally for nehalem). It passes `--version` and `process.stderr.fd` cleanly — but still SIGILLs/hangs under real load, because **JSC's JIT emits AVX at runtime**. A trivial JS loop hangs with the JIT on and runs instantly with it off. So a "baseline" build should be certified against a JIT-heavy workload, not just a startup smoke test.

Current working setup on the X5690:
- bun built from source (nehalem + local WebKit), run with `BUN_JSC_useJIT=0` → interpreted, no SIGILL. opencode 1.17.15 runs.
- The Go `opencode-cli` sidecar also SIGILLs even as `darwin-x64-baseline` (VEX-encoded AVX); rebuilding from source with `GOAMD64=v1 CGO_ENABLED=0` fixes that.
- Everything is cross-built on a newer host and copied to the old Mac.

**Offering our build.** I'm happy to publish this AVX-free build for download — the from-source nehalem `bun` binary plus the `GOAMD64=v1` `opencode-cli` — as a tagged GitHub release, or to feed the Westmere-verified binaries into @tobocop2's [pre-avx2-mac release repo](https://github.com/tobocop2/opencode-bun-pre-avx2-mac) so there's a single place people can grab a known-good no-AVX macOS build. Say which you'd prefer.

**Update procedure** (the part that actually matters day to day — the two components move at very different speeds):

1. **bun — slow, rare.** Rebuild from source only when bun's pinned version bumps, via a small unattended script (`--baseline=true --webkit=local`, ~1.5 h on a fast host; WebKit is the long pole). Until a build passes a *JIT-heavy* test it ships with `BUN_JSC_useJIT=0`. A release would pin the exact bun commit + WebKit commit so it's reproducible.
2. **opencode — fast, frequent.** opencode releases almost daily, and every prebuilt release re-introduces the AVX2 runtime, so you can't just let it auto-update. The working pattern is to run opencode *from source* on the nehalem bun: `git pull` the opencode source + `bun install`, then cross-ship to the old Mac. Nothing to recompile — the AVX-free bun is reused.
3. **Disable auto-update.** Same point @euxaristia made above: with auto-update on, opencode will happily pull an AVX2 prebuilt over your working copy and break it again. Pin the version / turn the updater off.

So the download would be: a rarely-changing AVX-free `bun` (the hard artifact) + instructions to track opencode from source against it. Happy to set that up and post the link here if there's interest.

Will report back either way once I've tested your prebuilt builds on the Westmere box — if they clear a no-AVX-at-all CPU they'll clear every AVX1 machine in this thread.

@tobocop2 Tested your `v1.18.1-baseline` build on a real pre-AVX Mac — **Mac Pro 5,1 (2010), Xeon X5690 Westmere, macOS 14.7.8**. CPU has `sse42 popcnt` only, no AVX/AVX2/BMI. Report below (both assets).

**SHA-256**
- `bun-darwin-x64-baseline` (60,733,504 B): `bede5eb3c917fa353d6b067fd7055d42774db7a7d5a09c21fa6cdd05e3d8efee`
- `opencode-darwin-x64-baseline` (103,282,752 B): `7daf210676d2efa9627619ab1823b141c861aa362f8a828db836472d9790e61f`

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun --version` | ✅ OK → `1.4.0`, no SIGILL |
| `process.stderr.fd` | ✅ OK → `2` |
| JIT-heavy loop (`for i<3e7: s+=Math.sqrt(i)`), **JIT ON** | ❌ **SIGILL (132)** — panic `Illegal instruction`, banner says *"CPU lacks AVX support"* |
| same loop, `BUN_JSC_useJIT=0` | ✅ OK |
| `opencode --version` | ❌ **SIGILL (132)** (JIT on at startup) |

**tl;dr — the startup half is fixed, the JIT half is not.**

The good news: the bmalloc/WebKit **startup-constructor** SIGILL is gone (`--version`, `process.stderr.fd` run clean), so your Nehalem WebKit artifact (WebKit#290) does its job for the pre-`main()` path. But **JSC's JIT still emits AVX at runtime**, so anything doing real work crashes. The crash banner itself prints `Features: jsc no_avx2 no_avx` and *"CPU lacks AVX support"* — i.e. it correctly detects there's no AVX, then emits AVX anyway. It only runs with `BUN_JSC_useJIT=0` (interpreted, slow).

Two things worth flagging:
1. Despite the `v1.18.1-baseline` tag, the binary self-reports as **`Bun Canary v1.4.0-canary.1 (1e3511800)`**, not 1.18.1.
2. The remaining fix probably isn't in WebKit's `-march` flags — it's JSC's JIT needing to gate VEX/AVX codegen on a runtime CPU check and fall back to SSE on Westmere/Nehalem. Right now `--baseline` + Nehalem WebKit fixes startup but the JIT tier is still unconditional AVX.

Happy to run more variants on this box if useful (it's a permanent no-AVX test machine).

After further investigation, this is expected behavior rather than an OpenCode bug.

A local variant named `max` does not implicitly set `reasoningEffort` to `max`. The correct configuration is:

```json
"max": {
  "reasoningEffort": "max"
}
```

With this explicit configuration, GPT-5.6 max reasoning works correctly in the reported setup. The `reasoning_options` field is model metadata used by the `models.dev` path; it is not the local `opencode.json` mechanism for configuring a variant.

Closing this issue as invalid.

That report nailed it, and your diagnosis was exactly right — it's the JIT, not the `-march` flags. I found the line and there's a build with the fix below.

`Source/JavaScriptCore/assembler/MacroAssemblerX86_64.cpp` at bun's pinned WebKit (`4895f45d`):

```cpp
#if OS(DARWIN)
        s_avxCheckState = CPUIDCheckState::Set;   // never checks the CPU
#else
        // CPUID.1:ECX.AVX[28] + OSXSAVE[27] + XCR0[2:1] == 11b
#endif
```

On macOS, JSC assumes AVX rather than asking. `supportsAVX()` then feeds ~10 VEX-emitting codegen sites. That's why your banner prints `no_avx` / "CPU lacks AVX support" and emits AVX anyway — bun's detection is right, JSC's is hardcoded past it. oven-sh/WebKit#198 fixed this exact bug for Linux/Windows in April and guarded the new code with `#if !OS(DARWIN)`, so Darwin kept the old assumption.

**I reproduced your SIGILL without a Westmere box** — an M1 running x86_64 bun under Rosetta 2, which also reports no AVX (`CPU: sse42 popcnt`). Identical to yours, which made this fast to iterate on:

| | your X5690 | M1 / Rosetta 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `bun --version` | rc=0 | rc=0 |
| JIT loop | **132** | **132** |
| `BUN_JSC_useJIT=0` | rc=0 | rc=0 |
| `opencode --version` | **132** | **132** |

**Build with the fix:** https://github.com/tobocop2/opencode-bun-pre-avx2-mac/releases/latest

```
873868a92fc1de5eb3bbae81a85e234186eb00f2b51da956e1835017d813d824  bun-darwin-x64-baseline
afe0fe21fc9b6ea43c33239aac990bb180c1025cc2d7044db5fab5ef4fc60915  opencode-darwin-x64-baseline
```

On Rosetta the JIT loop and `opencode --version` both go 132 → 0, and a 14-case suite (YarrJIT SIMD regex, strings/UTF-8, JSON, DFG/FTL tier-up, typed arrays) passes where the old build SIGILLs partway through. If it clears your X5690 too, that's a no-AVX-at-all CPU and it should cover every AVX1 machine in these threads.

Upstream: **oven-sh/WebKit#292**, tracked in oven-sh/bun#34215. Non-Darwin can't regress — the preprocessed output is byte-identical before/after (`6287bfdf…`), and on AVX hardware the new check returns `Set`, matching the old hardcode, so real AVX Macs are unchanged.

You were also right about the version. `v1.18.1-baseline` is opencode's version; the bun inside is built from bun `main` @ `1e35118008` and self-reports `1.4.0-canary.1` — not an official 1.3.14 baseline. I've said so plainly in the release now. Separately, `opencode --version` reported `0.0.0--<timestamp>` because cloning a tag leaves a detached HEAD and the version derivation falls back to a preview string; it reports `1.18.1` in this build.

Taking you up on the X5690 offer — Rosetta gets me a no-AVX macOS, but it isn't real Westmere silicon and the two could diverge.
